findings.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic-post.scss:263 — [P1, confidence 99] `@include flexbox();` turns the direct `button` child into a flex item, for which its existing `float: right` is ignored, so the action control is laid out immediately after the description instead of at the right edge; retaining the float rule does not preserve the prior layout because floats are disabled on flex items.

app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:118 — [P2, confidence 100] `-webkit-box-align: $alignment;` accompanies the emitted `display: -moz-box` fallback but no `-moz-box-align`, so legacy Gecko ignores every requested cross-axis alignment and renders the fallback layout with default stretching; the presence of the unprefixed declaration does not remedy a browser that selects `-moz-box`.

app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:126 — [P2, confidence 96] `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: $val;` exposes modern zero-based `order` values directly to the legacy one-based box ordinal API, so a consumer calling `@include order(1)` remains in the default legacy group while moving after default-order siblings in modern flexbox; the current `order(3)` use appearing later does not make the shared mixin's API semantically equivalent.

app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic-post.scss:264 — [P1, confidence 100] `@include flexbox();` turns each direct `.small-action button` into a flex item, causing its existing `float: right` declaration to be ignored and rendering the action immediately after the description rather than at the right edge.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:118 — [P3, confidence 100] `-webkit-box-align: $alignment;` — `inline-flex()` emits `display: -moz-inline-box` but `align-items()` never emits `-moz-box-align`, so Gecko using that supplied fallback ignores the requested baseline alignment and misaligns bullet badges.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a real inconsistency in the flexbox mixins. Looking at the diff, `inline-flex()` includes `-moz-inline-box` and `-moz-box` prefixes for old Gecko/Firefox support, but `align-items()` only includes `-webkit-box-align`, `-webkit-align-items`, `-ms-flex-align`, `-ms-align-items`, and standard `align-items` - it's missing `-moz-box-align`. This means if an old Firefox version uses the `-moz-inline-box` fallback from `inline-flex()`, the alignment from `align-items()` won't work because there's no corresponding `-moz-box-align` property. The bullet badges use both `@include inline-flex()` and `@include align-items(baseline)`, so this is a real compatibility bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:118 — [P2, confidence 100] `-webkit-box-align: $alignment;` — When a legacy Gecko browser selects the emitted `display: -moz-box` fallback, this mixin omits the required `-moz-box-align`, so `@include align-items(center)` silently falls back to stretch and breaks the header’s cross-axis layout; the later unprefixed declaration cannot apply in that browser.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the `@mixin align-items($alignment)` mixin at lines 115-121 includes `-webkit-box-align`, `-webkit-align-items`, `-ms-flex-align`, `-ms-align-items`, and `align-items`, but does NOT include `-moz-box-align`. Since the `@mixin flexbox()` includes `display: -moz-box` as a fallback (line 100), legacy Firefox browsers using that display mode would need `-moz-box-align` for cross-axis alignment to work. The finding correctly identifies this missing vendor prefix, which could cause alignment issues in legacy Gecko browsers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic-post.scss:263 — Adding flex layout and changing `.small-action-desc` spacing modifies topic-post small-action rendering even though the stated task is limited to optimizing the header layout, so this unrelated UI change bypasses the task's scope and review intent.

This is a scope/intent judgment that cannot be verified as a defect from the diff alone.
